cards.explanation: The picture is a rock, friends. The LORD says, “Look to the rock from which you were cut, and to the quarry from which you were hewn.” Stone, cut out of a quarry. He's telling them to look back at where they came from.
The answer is Abraham. The LORD says, “Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave you birth.” Notice he doesn't send them to Abraham alone. Sarah gets named right beside him, and I love that.

The LORD blessed him and multiplied him. He says, “…he was but one; then I blessed him and multiplied him.” One man became way more than one man. That's a big jump, friends, and the LORD is the one who did it.

The answer is Eden. The verse says the LORD “…will make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of the LORD.” Eden is where the LORD God planted a garden (Genesis 2:8). So Zion's dry, empty places get a whole garden picture.

The answer is False. The LORD will comfort Zion, and the verse says, “Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and melodious song.” That's the sound after the comfort, friends. Singing, not mourning.

The answer is LAW, bakers! The LORD says, “…a law will go out from Me, and My justice will become a light to the nations…” The law heads out the door, and His justice flips the lights on for the nations. That's the whole line, and it's a bright one.

The answer is True, and I LOVE how plain it is. The LORD lays out His law and His justice as a light to the nations. Then He says, “I will bring it about quickly.” No small print, no "terms and conditions apply." Just a promise, friends, and He means it.
The answer is that they look for Him and wait in hope. The verse says, “The islands will look for Me and wait in hope for My arm.” Looking and waiting in hope. Far-off places are watching for Him.

The answer is salvation. The LORD says, “But My salvation will last forever, and My righteousness will never fail.” The heavens vanish and the earth wears out, but His salvation stays put. That's a big comfort to hold onto, friends.

The answer is that moths will eat them like a garment. The LORD says, “For the moth will devour them like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool.” Moths and worms eat cloth, so the picture is easy to see. And right after it, His righteousness lasts forever.

The answer is a road for the redeemed to cross over. The speaker asks, “Was it not You who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made a road in the depths of the sea for the redeemed to cross over?” A road, right through the deep. The redeemed walked across.

The answer is everlasting joy. The verse says the redeemed “…will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy.” That's a crown I'd wear all day, friends. Gladness and joy overtake them, too.
The answer is False. The verse says, “Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.” Joy is the one catching up with them, friends. Sorrow is the one running off.
The answer is grass. The LORD says, “Why should you be afraid of mortal man, of a son of man who withers like grass?” Grass turns brown and gives out. So why fear what withers?

The answer is that they live in terror all day long. The LORD says, “You live in terror all day long because of the fury of the oppressor who is bent on destruction.” It's a heavy picture of living afraid. And it comes right after they've forgotten their Maker.

The answer is freed. The LORD says, “The captive will soon be freed; he will not die in the dungeon, and his bread will not be lacking.” Out of the dungeon, not stuck in it. And it says soon, friends.
The answer is True. The verse ends with, “…and his bread will not be lacking.” Out of the dungeon, and not going hungry. The LORD covers both, friends.

The LORD says, “You are My people.” The verse says, “I have put My words in your mouth, and covered you with the shadow of My hand…” and it ends with “…to say to Zion, ‘You are My people.’…” After all the promises, that's what He says to Zion. It's a warm place to land, friends.
